extracted.intended_audience: literary-minded readers — writers, actors/performers, and editors
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance for depicting character and conduct (in fiction or social portraiture) and for editorial treatment of texts — drawn from essays on dancing, conversation, public trust, acting, and textual editing. Useful for creative writers shaping character by action and for editors choosing variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion and change of Posture and Aspect
rubrics_metrics.description: Motion, and change of Posture and Aspect, has an Effect no less surprising on the Person of Mariamne when she Dances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bodily motion, posture, and changes of aspect to reveal character and alter the reader's/viewer's perception; movement can heighten beauty, introduce dignity, or expose folly. Example: the same face can be transformed by different attitudes or dress; performance should exploit posture to communicate inner qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dance as method to implant good breeding and virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Art was under proper Regulations, it would be a mechanick way of implanting insensibly in Minds ... a Sense of good Breeding and Virtue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat ritualized social arts (dance, ceremony) as tools that naturally inculcate manners and self-respect — in fiction, scenes of regulated social performance can plausibly show a character's acquisition of dignity and social worth. Also implies authors should depict regulated form producing moral as well as aesthetic effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good dancing requires good understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: No one ever was a good Dancer, that had not a good Understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link physical skill or graceful performance to intelligence and taste in characterization: foolish, frivolous behavior should be signaled by clumsy or senseless movement; conversely, refined movement implies reflection and self-command. Anti-pattern: portraying extreme physical nimbleness as divorced from mental acuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance vs performer: distinguish art's worth from perverse execution
rubrics_metrics.description: The flippant insipidly Gay and wantonly Forward, whom you behold among Dancers, that Carriage is more to be attributed to the perverse Genius of the Performers, than imputed to the Art it self.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When critiquing or depicting an art form, separate defects of individual performers from the intrinsic merits of the art. In practice, show how training/ regulation restores the art's dignity; avoid condemning a form wholesale because of vulgar practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reveal latent moral qualities through a brief performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Shewed in one Quarter of an Hour the innate Principles of a modest Virgin, a tender Wife, a generous Friend, a kind Mother, and an indulgent Mistress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concise scene of behavior (e.g., a dance, a social ritual) to reveal multiple, deep-seated moral traits quickly and economically. This is a device for efficient characterization: a short, well-chosen public action can display private virtues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes of an admirable gentleman (Manilius)
rubrics_metrics.description: Liberality in another... genteel, plain, and unaffected dress... first engages your Eye... looks with disdain on those who propose their Death as the Time when they are to begin their Munificence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When creating or evaluating an admirable public figure, emphasize: generous but prudent liberality, unaffected plainness of manner/dress, capacity to please across factions, private virtue matching public reputation, and the ability to brighten others without ostentation. Use anecdotes to demonstrate these attributes rather than didactic assertion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mix of gaiety and instruction in conversation
rubrics_metrics.description: The Gravity of his Conversation is always enlivened with his Wit and Humour, and the Gaiety of it is tempered with something that is instructive, as well as barely agreeable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft conversational passages (or portray conversational characters) so wit and amusement coexist with moral or instructive content; avoid being merely jocular at the expense of reason, or overly serious without charm. Balance is a hallmark of engaging social dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualities of a great conversationalist/actor (Eastcourt)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exquisite a Discerning of what was defective... in an Instant he could shew you the ridiculous Side of what would pass for beautiful... inimitable Faculty of telling a Story... would throw in natural and unexpected Incidents... vary the Usage he gave them, according as he saw them bear kind or sharp Language... would in his Narration fall into their very Way of thinking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For writers of comic characters or actors within fiction: develop the capacity to expose pretension, to tell stories with well-placed surprises, to adapt tone to audience, and to mimic both gesture and thought. Such performers combine keen observation of defects with humane comic tact; avoid cruel caricature and aim for insight that amuses while instructing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not let rank or circumstances define a man's character
rubrics_metrics.description: It is an Insolence natural to the Wealthy, to affix... the Character of a Man to his Circumstances. Thus it is ordinary with them to praise faintly the good Qualities of those below them...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When portraying characters, resist conflating social station with intrinsic merit; show virtues and talents through action and speech rather than through assumed status. Anti-pattern: using wealth or office as shorthand for moral worth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualifications for public office: temper and integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: A Man is unfit for such a Place of Trust, who is of a sower untractable Nature... proud Man discourages... impatient Man will not give himself time... Dilatory Temper... commits innumerable Cruelties without Design... there is no Man so improper... as he who is in any degree capable of Corruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For creating credible officers of state or judging their fitness: require compassion and benevolence, gentleness in manner, patience, promptness (avoid dilatoriness), and incorruptibility (no gratuities or extra fees). Scenes should illustrate these qualities (or their absence) by concrete acts: listening patiently, timely dispatch, refusal of illicit gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness as moral obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: Never to think of doing that To-morrow which may be done To-day. A Man who defers doing what ought to be done, is guilty of Injustice so long as he defers it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depict or evaluate characters' moral worth partly by their promptness in attending obligations: procrastination causes real injury and is ethically blameworthy. In plot or character arcs, use delay as a believable source of harm or conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial principle: note variants only when they affect sense or elegance
rubrics_metrics.description: When a different Reading gives us a different Sense, or a new Elegance in an Author, the Editor does very well in taking Notice of it; but when he only entertains us with the several ways of spelling the same Word... they only take up the Time of the learned Reader, and puzzle the Minds of the Ignorant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should favor variants that change meaning, metre, or aesthetic effect; avoid exhaustive lists of trivial orthographic differences. Use criteria such as impact on sense, metre/rhyme, and stylistic elegance when choosing which emendations or variant readings to print. Provide concise justification (meter, rhyme, sense) when selecting among competing readings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer readings that preserve metre and sense; weigh authorities contextually
rubrics_metrics.description: There are but two Reasons which incline me to the Reading as I have published it; First, because the Rhime, and, Secondly, because the Sense is preserved by it... several Manuscripts read differently, but rhyme and sense decide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When textual witnesses conflict, prioritize readings that retain a poem's metre and rhyme and preserve coherent sense; consider scribal errors (e.g., omitted cyphers, misread dashes) as plausible explanations. Explain editorial choices briefly and leave highly uncertain cases to learned debate rather than exhaustive conjecture.
